# OpenCode (terminal)

This host keeps its config in the project folder, so the setup travels with the repo.

## Install

```
headwaters install --host opencode
```

The installer prints the diff first and writes only after a yes; `--dry-run` stops at the
diff and `--json` prints the same plan as a document.

## Files

| File | What the install does |
| --- | --- |
| `<project>/opencode.json` | create |
| `<project>/AGENTS.md` | create |
| `<project>/.opencode/commands/headwaters-auto.md` | create |
| `<project>/.opencode/commands/headwaters-free.md` | create |
| `<project>/.opencode/commands/headwaters-handoff.md` | create |
| `<project>/.opencode/commands/headwaters-local.md` | create |
| `<project>/.opencode/commands/headwaters-status.md` | create |

## What you still do

- OpenCode reads the gateway token from HEADWATERS_TOKEN when it starts the provider: set it to the daemon token, or run `opencode auth login` and paste the token there.
- Models appear as headwaters/auto, /free and /local - the ids the picker names, so `--model` and /models agree.
- Commands live in .opencode/commands and take arguments with $ARGUMENTS.

## Templates behind this page

The entries above are rendered from `opencode` in `headwaters/installer/templates/`, so this page and a real install cannot drift.

## Check it

```
headwaters doctor --host opencode
```

The doctor reads this host's own config back and reports a missing or stale entry; a
clean report means the host is talking to the gateway.

## Remove it

```
headwaters uninstall --host opencode
```

The uninstall restores the backed-up file unless it was edited after the install; then it
asks for `--force`.
